The State Housing Company Limited (SHC) has rejected claims that its planned recovery of the land occupied by Sandbox Beach Club is politically motivated, insisting that the exercise forms part of a broader effort to reclaim state properties and enforce tenancy agreements.
The company's Public Relations Officer, Ewura Adams Karim, said the recovery exercise applied to all occupants of SHC-owned properties, irrespective of their political affiliations or the nature of their businesses.
His comments follow the marking of the Sandbox premises on Saturday, November 14, with a notice warning occupants and members of the public to keep off the property as part of the planned recovery exercise.
In a post on X on Sunday, November 15, Mr Karim dismissed suggestions that the beach club had been singled out because of its perceived political connections.
He said SHC had served notices on occupants of its properties, giving them 21 days to regularise their tenancy arrangements, renew expired leases or surrender vacant possession.
The company had also introduced a 15 per cent discount for occupants with outstanding payments to encourage them to settle their debts and bring their tenancy arrangements up to date, he added.
Mr Karim acknowledged concerns about the potential impact of the planned demolition on employees and their families but maintained that the company had given occupants sufficient notice and an opportunity to resolve their tenancy issues.
“We share the concern for workers and their families. That is exactly why SHC gave notice and offered the option to regularise. Protecting jobs and protecting public assets are not opposites,” he said.
He maintained that state-owned lands were public assets belonging to all Ghanaians and that efforts to reclaim them should not be construed as political persecution.
The company's response follows concerns raised by Richard Gyamfi, a member of the New Patriotic Party's National Communications Team, who questioned the basis for the planned demolition.
Sandbox Beach Club is owned by Sarah O. Femi Bediatuo, wife of Nana Asante Bediatuo, a cousin of former President Nana Addo Dankwa Akufo-Addo and his former Executive Secretary.
Sarah O. Femi Bediatuo is also the Chief Executive Officer of Hospitality Groupe Sebastien, the company responsible for managing the beach club.
